newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Tel Aviv exchange to set date for continuous trade.
newsitem.headline: Tel Aviv exchange to set date for continuous trade.

text.p: The board of directors of the Tel Aviv Stock Exchange (TASE) is scheduled to meet on Thursday to set a new date for the start of computerised continuous trading, a spokeswoman said on Tuesday.
"On Thursday this week the directors will make a decision when it will be implemented," Etti Tutnauer said.
The $4.25 million trading system was originally set to go into operation in March and then postponed to April.
Ester Levanon, executive vice president for information systems and administration at TASE, said the new system would probably be introduced in late June or early July.
Levanon attributed the delay to TASE's decision to widen the system to enable commercial banks to relay trading information through their computer networks to branches around the country.
"There haven't been any special technical problems," Tutnauer said, adding that the exchange was conducting daily tests of the system.

The system originally was going to reach only as far as the banks' dealing rooms. Although non-bank brokers will also be linked to the network, the banks' brokerage arms account for most of the brokerage activity on TASE.
Levanon denied newspaper reports that the system had failed in trials and said there were no technical barriers to its introduction.
The new system will initially be used to trade about 10 stocks from the Mishtanim list of top 100 shares and after a month of trials expanded to the blue chip shares of the Maof 25 index, she said.
Small capitalisation stocks might eventually be traded continuously as well, she added, but for short periods at a time.
TASE now uses a system it calls "semi-continuous trading" for its heavy capitalisation shares. The new system is aimed at making the TASE more closely resemble trading systems elsewhere in the world.
